source.title: Implicit Regularization in Over-Parameterized Support Vector Machine
source.authors: Yang Sui; Xin He; Yang Bai

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Extends implicit-regularization experiments to sparse SVM classification and reports held-out prediction results; it does not test any listed version directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out prediction accuracy for its SVM methods, but does not report training error or a train–test gap, random-label memorization, or any of the specific interventions or measurements in V1–V8.
record.test_reason: The study develops and evaluates implicit regularization in reparameterized sparse linear SVMs. Its parameter-recovery guarantees and synthetic-data prediction comparisons do not test any of V1–V8. Overparameterization alone does not establish random-label memorization or continued improvement beyond an interpolation width threshold.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors establish near-oracle parameter-estimation rates for an unpenalized, reparameterized and smoothed sparse SVM under incoherence and suitable initialization, step size, smoothing, and stopping conditions. Simulations show competitive prediction and improved estimation and variable selection relative to ℓ1 regularization. The theoretical rate concerns parameter recovery, rather than a training–test gap or prediction-accuracy guarantee.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a Hadamard-product re-parameterization of sparse SVM parameters and Nesterov smoothing; experiments use synthetic data and compare with ℓ1 regularization and an oracle.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization size, signal strength, sample size, signal structure, input distribution, and smoothing parameter are varied in the simulations.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed reparameterized SVM achieves high held-out prediction accuracy, outperforms the ℓ1-regularized comparator in several synthetic settings, and approaches the support-informed oracle.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Suitably configured gradient descent on a reparameterized sparse SVM can provide effective implicit regularization on synthetic classification tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 2 bounds squared parameter-estimation error by a constant times s log(p)/n under design and initialization assumptions, with suitable step size, smoothing, and an iteration count within a specified interval.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reparameterized gradient descent can achieve near-oracle sparse-SVM parameter recovery without an explicit penalty under the stated assumptions and stopping conditions.

record.peer_reviewed: Neural Information Processing Systems (2023, as given in the source metadata); paper text identifies itself as a preprint under review.
record.problems: Experiments use generated data rather than natural datasets. Prediction results are primarily in figures, with no exact accuracy values in the prose; no training-error results or train–test gaps are reported.

untested.parts: No fixed random-label fitting experiment or paired natural-label and random-label held-out evaluation.
No neural-network width sweep, interpolation threshold, or test-error trend beyond that threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
No adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparison or optimizer-tuning experiment.
No batch-size comparison under controlled epoch budgets or adapted training recipes.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement, generalization-gap ranking, or comparison with norm and margin measures.
No memorization-based example selection, removal, and retraining comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The paper cites original sources associated with V2, V4, and V5 as background on implicit regularization; it does not reproduce their claim-specific tests. The row states indicate that these measures cannot determine any listed version, rather than uncertainty about whether the reported SVM prediction results occurred.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of natural-label and random-label held-out performance.
No one-hidden-layer ReLU width sweep or test-error analysis past the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
